Cirrus Logic Faces Pricing Pressure: Can Gross Margin Stay Firm?
Cirrus Logic, Inc. CRUS reported a non-GAAP gross margin of 52.7% for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, alongside non-GAAP gross profit of $242.1 million. The margin declined sequentially, primarily reflecting previously expected pricing reductions, although cost cuts partially offset the impact. Compared with the year-ago quarter, gross margin increased slightly, mainly due to a favorable product mix, partly offset by higher freight and supply-chain costs. The company also highlighted that anticipated pricing reductions partially offset year-over-year revenue growth.
For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Cirrus Logic expects GAAP gross margin between 52% and 54%. On the last earnings call, management stated that the quarter should receive a temporary benefit from wafers purchased under prior agreements with GlobalFoundries at favorable pricing. However, this tranche of lower-cost wafers is expected to largely sell through during the fiscal second quarter, after which gross margin is expected to normalize.
During the earnings call, management reiterated its long-term gross-margin outlook despite ongoing discussion around input costs across the supply chain. The company noted that many of the costs currently flowing through its results had been agreed upon well in advance and were therefore coming through largely as expected. At the same time, the company continues to monitor input-cost developments closely. To address potential pressure, management said it will aggressively pursue cost reductions and consider targeted price increases where warranted.
Supply-chain conditions remain an important consideration. Cirrus recently entered into a new capacity reservation and wafer supply agreement with GlobalFoundries that secures dedicated wafer capacity and pricing for calendar years 2027 and 2028. In addition, the company highlighted that newly developed products for smart-meter and adjacent applications are expected to carry gross margins well above the corporate average, while also broadening its addressable market.
Overall, Cirrus is managing previously anticipated pricing reductions, higher freight and supply-chain costs and broader input-cost uncertainty while maintaining its long-term gross-margin outlook and guiding second-quarter gross margin to 52-54%.
Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM faces mounting earnings risk as handset weakness, lower Apple modem share and rising input costs weigh on QCT profitability. Memory-driven demand pressure and customer mix shifts are constraining mobile, while price increases will take time to offset higher wafer, assembly, test and packaging costs. Data center expansion also carries execution risk because near-term custom silicon revenue is expected to dilute QCT gross margins before the platform reaches scale. Elevated spending on new compute programs and debt above cash and marketable securities further limit flexibility. Qualcomm's QCT EBT margin declined to 26% from 30% as higher product costs offset higher average selling prices. For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the company expects QCT EBT margin of 23-25% and total revenue of $9.7-$10.5 billion.
Skyworks Solutions, Inc. SWKS is benefiting from sustained Broad Markets growth, led by Wi-Fi adoption, automotive connectivity and data center timing and power products. Rising RF complexity and a multi-generational Android win support the Mobile content outlook, while the Qorvo combination could add scale, diversification and cost savings. Near-term demand remains steady, and the fall smartphone ramp should lift Mobile revenue. For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Skyworks expects revenues to be between $1.01 billion and $1.06 billion. Mobile revenues are expected to grow sequentially in the high teens, driven by seasonal product launches at the largest customer. Broad Markets is projected to increase approximately 5% year over year and represent about 39% of sales. The company anticipates gross margin between 44% and 45%.
CRUS Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates
Shares of CRUS have lost 18% in the past three months compared with the Electronics-Semiconductors industry's decline of 12.4%.
CRUS is trading at a forward 12-month price/earnings ratio of 15.98, higher than the Electronics-Semiconductors sector's multiple of 13.93.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CRUS' earnings for fiscal 2027 has been revised downward over the past 60 days.

Cirrus Logic Announces Acquisition of INVENTVM Semiconductor
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 1:00 PM PDT 3 min read
AUSTIN, Texas, October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cirrus Logic, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRUS) announced that it has acquired INVENTVM, a fabless semiconductor company based in Pavia, Italy that specializes in mixed-signal power management and audio integrated circuits. INVENTVM brings deep engineering expertise, intellectual property, and an established presence in a region where Cirrus Logic intends to expand further. This acquisition enables Cirrus Logic to accelerate the development of industry-leading products, supporting the company's long-term growth strategy to expand into additional applications and markets.
"Our current pipeline of opportunities is the strongest we've ever had, and this acquisition directly adds innovative IP, expands our engineering capacity, increases our talent depth, and supports our efforts to grow in new applications and markets," said John Forsyth, Cirrus Logic president and chief executive officer. "Having worked together closely for several years, we know the strength of this team, and we look forward to them joining our world-class engineering organization."
"This announcement reflects the strong relationship our teams have built over many years of collaboration," said Michele Chiabrera, chief executive officer of INVENTVM. "We are proud of what the INVENTVM team has accomplished, and we believe joining Cirrus Logic will create new opportunities to advance our technology, support customers, and continue innovating as part of a larger global organization."
The financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed, and the transaction will not have a material impact on Cirrus Logic's revenue.
Cirrus Logic is a leader in low-power, high-precision mixed-signal processing solutions that create innovative user experiences for the world's top mobile and consumer applications. With headquarters in Austin, Texas, Cirrus Logic is recognized globally for its award-winning corporate culture.

bull_case: Cirrus Logic acquired INVENTVM, an Italy-based fabless semiconductor firm specializing in mixed-signal power management. The acquisition enables Cirrus Logic to accelerate development of industry-leading products and expand into new applications and markets. INVENTVM brings deep engineering expertise, intellectual property, and an established presence in a region where Cirrus Logic intends to expand. Cirrus Logic's CEO John Forsyth stated the acquisition adds innovative IP, expands engineering capacity, increases talent depth, and supports growth in new markets. INVENTVM's CEO Michele Chiabrera noted the acquisition creates opportunities to advance technology, support customers, and continue innovating within a larger organization. The acquisition does not have a material impact on Cirrus Logic's revenue. Cirrus Logic's revenue reached USD 459.72 million in Q1 fiscal 2027, with 12.90% year-over-year growth. Cirrus Logic expects GAAP gross margin between 52% and 54% for Q2 fiscal 2027. Cirrus Logic entered into a new wafer supply agreement with GlobalFoundries for calendar years 2027 and 2028. Cirrus Logic's newly developed smart-meter products are expected to carry gross margins well above the corporate average.
bear_case: CRUS shares have lost 18% in the past three months compared to the Electronics-Semiconductors industry's decline of 12.4%. CRUS is trading at a forward 12-month P/E ratio of 15.98, higher than the sector's multiple of 13.93. Zacks Consensus Estimate for CRUS' fiscal 2027 earnings has been revised downward over the past 60 days. CRUS has a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). Cirrus Logic identifies changes in orders and shipments, general market conditions, and customer concentration as business risks.
